justification: Adds the exact wording of NSW Road Rules 2014 regs 231, 232 and 234 (pasted by the user from AustLII on 2026-11-20) as saved law data, and shows four quotes (231(2), 232(2), 234(1), 234(4)) on the evidence page beside the crossings-only walk line, with the clause, the source address and 'shown for reference; this tool does not decide whether a walk is lawful'. Nothing is paraphrased: each quote is cut word for word from the saved text, and the evidence data refuses to serve a quote that is not found word for word in that text, or a text whose fingerprint changed (status unreadable). Also copies the two data files into the Python image (Dockerfile.python) so production can read them. No query, no schema.

falsifiable_check.command: python -m pytest tests/test_evidence_statement.py tests/test_lmr_data_files.py -q -o addopts= ; cd frontend-nextjs && npx jest __tests__/components/evidence-statement-page.test.tsx
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Three hand mutations each turned tests red and were restored: changing one word of a stored quote (3 Python tests fail), deleting the Docker COPY line for the road-rules file (test_the_python_image_copies_every_file_the_area_check_reads fails), and showing the road rules without a crossings-only line (1 Jest test fails). Restored: Python 53 passed, Jest 15 passed, tsc 0 errors.
falsifiable_check.fails_when: A stored quote differs from the saved text, the saved text no longer matches its fingerprint, the image stops copying the files, or the page shows the rules without a crossings-only line.

pre_impl.existing_data: data/law holds the Housing SEPP facts and text with a text_file + text_sha256 + clause + quote pattern (extract_lmr_law_facts.text_sha256 ignores line-ending differences). This follows it; the fingerprint is checked against that same function.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: AustLII and legislation.nsw.gov.au return HTTP 403 to automated downloads, so the text could not be fetched by a script. The user copied it from a browser and pasted it; the saved header says so and that the page gives no consolidation date.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: New: two data files, one loader (road_rules) and one optional key (road_rules) on the evidence data. Existing evidence parts are untouched.
pre_impl.external_source_error: None at run time: no network call. A missing, altered or fingerprint-mismatched file gives status 'unreadable' with a reason, never a crash and never a changed quote.
pre_impl.frontend_type: road_rules is optional on the page (Vercel and Railway deploy separately) and a wrong shape fails visibly in isEvidence.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: A planner never sees a paraphrase presented as the rule. If the wording cannot be verified the page says it could not be shown.

functions.name: road_rules
functions.input: path of the facts file and the repo root (both defaulted)
functions.output: status ok with the quotes, clause, heading and source address, or status unreadable with a reason
functions.if_none: A missing file, bad JSON, wrong fingerprint, missing field or a quote not found word for word all give status unreadable; it never raises and never returns a quote it could not verify.

functions.name: EvidenceStatement
functions.input: lat and lng from the address bar
functions.output: the printable evidence page with the road rules shown only beside a crossings-only line
functions.if_none: No road_rules key (an older server) shows nothing; status unreadable shows a plain sentence.

values.value: quote, clause and source_url of each road rule
values.if_missing: status unreadable; the page says the wording could not be shown.
Left out; an older server answer still renders.

break_it.scenario: Someone edits a stored quote (for example 'must not cross' to 'may cross').
break_it.what_happens: road_rules() returns unreadable naming the clause; the page says the wording could not be shown.
break_it.mitigated: Mitigated: every quote must be found word for word in the saved text before it is served, and tests check the committed file.
break_it.how: The word-for-word check in road_rules() and the committed-file test.

break_it.scenario: The saved text file is edited or replaced.
break_it.what_happens: Its fingerprint no longer matches and road_rules() returns unreadable.
break_it.mitigated: Mitigated: sha256 over the line-ending-normalised text, the same function the Housing SEPP facts use.

break_it.scenario: The Python image does not copy the two data files.
break_it.what_happens: Production would report the road rules as unreadable.
break_it.mitigated: Mitigated: Dockerfile.python copies both and a test requires the COPY lines.

break_it.scenario: The lot has no crossings-only line.
break_it.what_happens: The road rules are not shown; they are only shown beside that line.
break_it.mitigated: Mitigated: the page shows them only when a crossings-only note or distance is present.
break_it.how: The condition in the page and its Jest test.

post_merge.manual_verify: After both the Python API and the front end deploy, open /reports/evidence-statement?lat=-33.735496841364196&lng=151.13852529738543 (28 Selwyn Street, Pymble): under the crossings-only line the four quotes, clauses and AustLII addresses should show. Also curl the evidence API and check road_rules.status is 'ok' (not 'unreadable', which would mean the image lacks the files).
